title: Canonical Tate, zero-section integration, and section restriction comparisons
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum $P$ of [def-pur-conventions] and the specified Tate twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. This definition names five canonical restriction and zero-section comparison constructions, with the ordinary/pro-etale site comparison and pullback compositors of [def-pur-section-pullback-site-comparisons]. It does not assert that a diagonal orientation equals inverse integration.

For every morphism of schemes $h:T\to S$, let $\operatorname{pull}(h)$ be the actual small pro-etale derived inverse-image functor at $P$'s finite coefficients [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. For a map $a_S:S\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $d\in\mathbf N$, let $\operatorname{tate}(h,a_S,d):Lh^*(A_S(d)[2d])\xrightarrow{\sim}A_T(d)[2d]$ be the canonical comparison of $Lh^*$ with the ordinary-etale site comparison, followed by that comparison's image of the ordinary finite Tate coefficient-pullback isomorphism [def-amb-vector-integration-charts]. These are the specified Cartesian Tate transports [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-twists], including the ordered even shifts.

For a finite-type scheme $B\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and a rank-$d$ locally free module $F$, let $\pi:\mathbf V(F)\to B$ and $z:B\to\mathbf V(F)$ be its bundle and zero section [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]. Define $\operatorname{vectorBetaInverse}:A_B(d)[2d]\to Lz^*R\pi^!\mathbf1_B$ as follows in the ordinary etale presentation. First use the inverse Tate pullback along $z$; then pull along $z$ the composite of the inverse Tate pullback along $\pi$ and the exceptional adjunction transpose of the actual integration map of [def-amb-vector-integration], followed by the canonical degree-zero-coefficient-to-tensor-unit comparison. Thus it is the actual integration adjunct pulled to zero, with its canonical Tate source identification, before taking any inverse. The exceptional functors are those of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image].

For separated finite-type morphisms $g:T\to S$ and $g':T'\to S'$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], with $g$ smooth of pure relative dimension $d$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], finite-type maps $a_S:S\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $a_{S'}:S'\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, a Cartesian square $(v:T'\to T,b:S'\to S)$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and maps $s:S\to T$, $s':S'\to T'$ satisfying $v\circ s'=s\circ b$, define the section exchange $Lb^*C(g,s)\xrightarrow{\sim}C(g',s')$ [def-pur-section-invariant] by the canonical commutation of pullback with the site comparison, followed by the comparison image of ordinary section base change. The latter is the section pullback of the smooth exceptional exchange, with its canonical inverse-image composition constraints.

Finally, for any scheme map $f:X\to Y$ and opens $V'\subseteq V\subseteq Y$ [def-weil-open-immersion], define the inclusion of inverse-image opens $f^{-1}V'\to f^{-1}V$ to be the actual open inclusion induced by $f^{-1}V'\subseteq f^{-1}V$. All five constructions are the existing canonical maps, including empty opens and $d=0$, and impose no absolute separatedness on a global base.
